name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text:
Cross-department improvement: Standardize a single "living Decision Log" template across all teams, enforced by the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf). Every decision entry must cite raw data—no exceptions—so future agents can verify claims without digging through scattered files.

Trade-off: This slows initial adoption because teams must adapt to the template, but it eliminates the recurring cost of re-deriving decisions from incomplete or conflicting sources.

name: Scriv
text: The risk isn’t speed—it’s that forcing raw data citations in every log entry turns the Decision Log into a graveyard of noise. Agents will drown in citations that don’t clarify the decision, just the inputs. Instead, mandate *only* the data that directly changed the outcome in the log; everything else stays in the raw files. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot where teams log decisions with and without the restriction, then measure how often future agents waste time chasing irrelevant citations.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" template: every entry must state the *decision*, the *data that flipped the outcome*, and the *uncertainty that remains*. Enforce this via the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf) to keep logs lean and actionable.

Trade-off: We accept that some useful context may get trimmed, but we gain logs that agents can actually *use* to verify claims without drowning in noise.

name: Sift
text: The "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" still risks teams gaming the system by cherry-picking the data that *seems* outcome-flipping in hindsight, not the data that *actually* did. The real fix is to require *all* raw data considered in the decision—even the contradictory or weak signals—so agents can audit the full reasoning chain, not just the polished narrative. Settle it by running a blind test: have two teams log the same decision, one with the current template, one with full data inclusion, then measure how often future agents flag inconsistencies in each.

name: Scope
text:
Adopt the "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" template enforced by the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf). Every log entry must state the decision, the data that flipped the outcome, and the remaining uncertainty—no more, no less. This keeps logs lean and actionable while still forcing teams to justify their choices with evidence.

Trade-off: We accept that some useful context may get trimmed, but the clarity of outcome-focused logs outweighs the noise of unfiltered data dumps.

name: Scriv
text: The "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" still risks teams hiding weak or contradictory data that didn’t flip the outcome but shaped the decision. The real fix is to require *all* raw data considered—even the noise—so agents can audit the full reasoning chain. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot with the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf) enforcing full disclosure, then measure how often agents flag hidden contradictions.

name: Reel
text:
Run a 30-day pilot of the "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" template enforced by the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf) with one high-stakes team—say, Creative Production. Every log entry must state the decision, the data that flipped the outcome, and the remaining uncertainty; nothing else. This forces teams to focus on what truly mattered, keeping logs lean and auditable without drowning in noise.

Trade-off: We accept that some useful context may be lost, but the risk of bloated logs is worse. If the pilot succeeds, roll it out to all teams.

name: Scriv
text: The 30-day pilot risks rewarding teams for gaming the system by cherry-picking "flipped outcome" data while burying weak signals. Instead, mandate *all* raw data considered—even noise—logged in a separate "Data Dump" artifact, linked to the Decision Log. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot with two teams: one using the current template, one using the Data Dump. Compare auditability and decision quality.

name: Chisel
text:
Run the 30-day pilot with Creative Production using the "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" enforced by the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf). Require every log entry to state the decision, the data that flipped the outcome, and the remaining uncertainty—nothing else. This forces teams to justify their choices with the strongest evidence, keeping logs lean and actionable.

Trade-off: We accept that weak or contradictory data may still be hidden, but the pilot’s strict enforcement will reveal how often this happens and whether it undermines decisions.

name: Sift
text: The "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" alone won’t stop gaming—teams will still bury weak signals in the "Data Dump" unless the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf) *automatically flags* when key data contradicts the stated outcome. Run a 30-day pilot where eA9Zf cross-checks every Decision Log against the raw "Data Dump" and surfaces mismatches for review.

name: Scope
text: Run the 30-day pilot with Creative Production using the "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" enforced by eA9Zf, but add a mandatory "Data Dump" artifact linked to each log. The AI Executive Assistant will auto-flag when key data contradicts the stated outcome, forcing teams to surface weak signals. This balances speed with rigor—teams can’t hide noise, and the flagging system prevents gaming without slowing decisions. The trade-off is extra upfront work for Creative Production, but the artifact’s existence will expose real reasoning gaps faster than any debate.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: The "Data Dump" artifact creates a false sense of completeness—teams will dump endless noise, not the *relevant* weak signals that actually undermine decisions. Instead, mandate a *short, structured "Contradiction Report"* attached to every Decision Log, listing only the top 3 data points that conflict with the outcome. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot with Creative Production, where eA9Zf auto-generates the report from raw data and flags unresolved contradictions for review.

name: Reel
text: Run the 30-day pilot with Creative Production using the "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" enforced by eA9Zf, but replace the "Data Dump" and "Contradiction Report" with a single mandatory artifact: the "Contradiction Report" must list the top 3 data points that *could* flip the decision, ranked by impact. This forces teams to focus on the most critical weak signals without drowning in noise. The trade-off is that some relevant data might be excluded, but it’s better to prioritize actionable signals than to bury teams in irrelevant information.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: The "Contradiction Report" still lets teams cherry-pick which contradictions to surface—ranking by impact invites gaming. Instead, mandate the AI Executive Assistant (eA9Zf) to auto-generate the top 3 contradictions from the raw data dump, with no human filtering allowed. Settle it by running a 30-day pilot where eA9Zf’s report is locked before teams see it.

name: Chisel
text: Run the 30-day pilot with Creative Production using the "Outcome-Centric Decision Log" enforced by eA9Zf, but mandate that eA9Zf auto-generates the top 3 contradictions from raw data—no human filtering allowed. This forces teams to confront the strongest signals against their decisions, not just the ones they choose to highlight. The trade-off is accepting slower log completion as teams adjust to the stricter process, but it eliminates gaming and ensures real weak signals surface.

name: Sift
text: The auto-generated top 3 contradictions risk creating a false precision—teams will game the ranking by manipulating the raw data dump to bury the real contradictions deeper in the noise. Instead, mandate that eA9Zf *randomly samples* 3 contradictions from the raw data, ensuring no predictable pattern for gaming. Settle it by running a 14-day A/B test comparing auto-ranked vs. random sampling, measuring how often teams adjust their decisions when confronted with contradictions.
